## Code Review Summary

**Mode:** Specification (staged). Candidate `header-parameter-transit-spec-r5` / r5. Bound inputs: `.scratch/header-parameter-transit/spec.md`, `issues/01`–`04`. Total issues: 6.

### By Severity
CRITICAL 0 / HIGH 0 / MEDIUM 2 / LOW 4

### CR3 closure
- **H1 CLOSED.** AC01-4 (spec.md:123) and AC03-1 (:130) assert one `server/discover`, zero `initialize`. `latestProtocolVersion` is `2026-07-28` (client.go:327,390; existing negotiation test `internal/upstream/runtime_test.go:150`), so the pinned peer negotiates on the first probe.
- **H2 CLOSED.** Tool unique ID is the name (server.go:261); `all()` sorts keys (features.go:103, page via `paginateList` server.go:2215). `aaa_control_tool` < `mmm_body_tool` < `zzz_header_tool` gives exactly 3 pages at `PageSize: 1`.
- **M1 CLOSED.** I5 (:111) and §4:105 scope deadline/cancel to `deadline_exceeded`/`internal_error` with `unknown`; the specified seam returns the prepare error before `RecordFailure`/`RecordSuccess` (runtime.go:204–231, 266/286). Zero accounting is structurally reachable.
- **M2 PARTIAL.** See F1.
- **M3 CLOSED.** `SetCacheable` (server.go:183, invoked at :1114) plus `cache.get` TTL semantics make the exact zero list delta feasible.
- **L1 CLOSED.** AC03-3 (:132) is six greps plus explicit content inspection.
- **L2 CLOSED.** T1 scope (:153) captures HTTP status and JSON-RPC error code of rejected requests.

### Issues
**[MEDIUM][HIGH] F1 — R2 remains absolute while I2 admits under-inclusion.**
spec.md:13 (R2) vs :111 (I2) and :95. R2 requires the index to "never disagree … in the under-inclusive direction for an already-published tool"; I2 permits the catalog to publish a header-bound tool the index lacks for one refresh interval, and §4 scopes the property to "each installation". A design invariant cannot narrow a requirement, so the CR3 M2 repair is textual-only in §4.
Fix: restate R2's last sentence as the snapshot-scoped guarantee (index contains every header-bound tool of the discovery it derives from; one interval of catalog lag stays body-only and is rejected before execution). No R/AC id, envelope or test change.

**[MEDIUM][HIGH] F2 — R1/R5 "exactly one execution" has no oracle.**
R1 (:11), R5 (:19), AC02-1 (:125), AC03-1 (:130). Neither success-path AC asserts the peer recorded exactly one `tools/call`; T1:156 records the count only as receipt evidence. A duplicate execution (transport retry) would pass every named oracle.
Fix: add "the peer records exactly one `tools/call` request" to AC02-1 and AC03-1.

**[LOW][HIGH] F3 — stale anchor.** spec.md:40 cites `cmd/mcp-bridge/wiring.go:142`; the facade is at `wiring.go:177–178`.

**[LOW][HIGH] F4 — stale anchor.** spec.md:33 and :254 cite `go.mod:11`; go-sdk v1.8.0 is `go.mod:8`.

**[LOW][HIGH] F5 — sequence contradicted by source.** spec.md:107 orders stateless calls "admission → connect"; `Dedicated.CallTool` connects at dedicated.go:377 and admits inside `ServerClient.CallTool` (runtime.go:190). The normative prepare-after-admission text is correct; fix the sequence line.

**[LOW][MEDIUM] F6 — timeout/range wording.** spec.md:103 says all RPCs share the call timeout; the stateless connect uses the parent context (`CallContext` starts at runtime.go:178/184). `put` is client.go:1276 (cited 1277–1300); `sortKeys` is features.go:100–104 (cited 76–99).

### Open Questions
- AC03-2 (:131) "probe rejected with `CodeUnsupportedProtocolVersion`": a legacy-pinned peer answers 200 with a legacy `DiscoverResult` (server.go:926–952; discover exempt at streamable.go:1526–1533) and the error is synthesized client-side (client.go:443–448). The fallback outcome is sound; confirm the test asserts the negotiated version, not a wire error. LOW.
- AC03-1's positive-TTL fixture needs a TTL comfortably longer than the test; "`TTLMs > 0`" alone permits expiry and would break the exact-zero assertion. LOW.

### Positive Observations
Modern-peer stateless transport, older-only legacy pin, argument retention and payload-free rejection are source-accurate; all write sets sit exactly inside `env-1`; every focused `-run` pattern matches its named oracle; deadline/cancel scoping is now explicit; no ticket criterion was weakened.

### Recommendation
REQUEST CHANGES
